html:
The Battle of Königgrätz, also called Sadowa, was fought on 3 July 1866 near Königgrätz, now Hradec Králové in the Czech Republic. The army of Prussia beat the army of the Austrian Empire and its ally Saxony. About 440,000 men took part.

The Prussian minister Otto von Bismarck wanted to push Austria out of German affairs and unite the north German states under Prussia. A quarrel over Schleswig and Holstein gave him his war. The Prussian chief of staff, Helmuth von Moltke, used railways and the telegraph to send three armies into Bohemia by separate routes and bring them together on the battlefield. Two of them attacked in the morning and were held by Austrian guns. In the afternoon the third hit the Austrian right side and the line gave way. The Prussian infantry's breech-loading rifles fired several times faster than the Austrian muzzle-loaders. Austria lost about 44,000 men, half of them prisoners. Prussia lost about 9,000.

The war was over in seven weeks. The German Confederation was dissolved and Austria left German politics. Prussia annexed several states and led a new north German union, which became the German Empire in 1871. Austria gave Venetia to Italy.
